prompt.brief: Design a multimodal conversational AI application that accepts text, images, and speech, retrieves grounded knowledge, understands intent, and answers users reliably at scale.
successSignals: Separate conversation state, tenant knowledge sources, document chunks, embeddings, prompts, and model outputs.
Keep p95 response latency below two seconds with bounded retrieval, token budgets, streaming output, and model fallbacks.
Ground answers in authorized knowledge and defend against prompt injection, data leakage, abuse, and hallucination.
Make model calls, tool calls, safety filters, evaluation, and usage accounting observable and retry-safe.

functional: Create assistants, upload authorized knowledge, and configure supported text, image, speech, tools, and model policies.
Accept a user turn, classify intent, retrieve relevant context, generate a cited response, and stream partial output.
Store conversation history, feedback, safety decisions, token usage, traces, and evaluation results with tenant isolation.
nonFunctional: Target p95 time to first token below 500 ms and p95 completed response below 2 seconds for normal turns.
Scale conversation traffic and embedding/index updates without unbounded prompt size or a hot tenant.
Do not lose committed turns or audit events; make model retries and tool calls idempotent where possible.
Degrade to a smaller model, cached retrieval, or an explicit unavailable response when dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: Support 100K concurrent conversations, 10K model requests per second, and millions of indexed documents.
Partition conversation state by tenant and conversation; shard embeddings by collection and isolate large tenants.
Bound history and retrieved context in prompts while retaining encrypted audit and evaluation data for replay.

dataFlow.title: Accept and persist the user turn
dataFlow.description: The gateway authenticates the tenant and user, enforces quotas, stores the user turn with an idempotency key, and creates a trace context.

dataFlow.title: Select context and tools
dataFlow.description: The orchestrator classifies intent, applies assistant policy, retrieves only authorized chunks, and selects tools within a bounded token and time budget.

dataFlow.title: Generate a grounded response
dataFlow.description: A model gateway calls the selected model with citations and safety instructions, streams tokens, validates tool results, and records the model version and usage.

dataFlow.title: Process knowledge and evaluation asynchronously
dataFlow.description: Workers chunk and embed documents, update the vector index, run safety and quality evaluations, and publish freshness and ingestion status without blocking chat responses.

dataFlow.title: Reconcile, audit, and recover asynchronously
dataFlow.description: The system records feedback, traces, moderation outcomes, and cost metrics; retries transient model calls and replays indexing from durable documents.

deepDives.title: Conversation and model consistency
points: Commit the user turn and assistant policy before generation; treat retrieval indexes and analytics as eventually consistent.
Use request IDs for turns, tool-call IDs for side effects, and model/version metadata for reproducible traces.
Return citations, safety status, model identity, and usage metadata so clients can explain the answer.

deepDives.title: Retrieval quality and prompt budgets
points: Partition conversation state by tenant and conversation, and vector indexes by assistant knowledge collection.
Retrieve a bounded top-k context, rerank it, and reject chunks that fail tenant, document, or user authorization.
Keep a replayable document pipeline and compare index versions when answers appear stale or ungrounded.

deepDives.title: Safety and dependency failure
points: Apply input, retrieval, tool, and output safety checks; never let retrieved instructions override system policy.
Fall back to a smaller model or retrieval-only answer when the primary model is unavailable, and never fabricate a successful tool action.
Measure time to first token, groundedness, refusal quality, token cost, retrieval freshness, and tenant-level error rates.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.

rubric.description: The answer defines the primary workflow, data model, scale, latency, durability, and failure contract.
Entities and keys support the primary access patterns, authorization, privacy, and lifecycle changes.
Partitioning, cache behavior, queues, backpressure, and hot-key handling are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded reads, and observability protect committed state.
The candidate can explain Multimodal conversational AI application consistency, push/pull, managed services, and the scale boundary.
